''' Wolfgang Steglich ''' (born 12 August 1933) is a German chemist.

==Life==
Wolfgang Steglich was born in [[Kamenz]] and studied chemistry at [[Technische Universität Berlin]] and later at the [[Technical University of Munich]] where he received his PhD in 1960 for work with {{ill|Friedrich Weygand|de}}. Following a postdoc stay with Sir [[Derek Barton|Derek H. R. Barton]] at the [[Imperial College London]], Wolfgang Steglich completed his [[habilitation]] at the Technical University of Munich. After Weygand's death in 1969,<ref>{{Cite journal
 | title = Nachruf Friedrich Weygand (mit Schriftenverzeichnis)
 | url=http://www.znaturforsch.com/ab/v25b/25b0126.pdf
 | pages = 126–133
 | author = Helmut Simon, Wolfgang Steglich
 | journal = Zeitschrift für Naturforschung
 | volume = 25B
 | issue = 2
 | year = 1970}}
</ref> Steglich was in charge of the Weygand chair until he became a full professor at Technische Universität Berlin in 1971. In 1975, he was appointed a professorship at the [[University of Bonn]]. He succeeded [[Rolf Huisgen]] as head of the organic chemistry department of [[LMU Munich]] in 1991. Wolfgang Steglich retired in 2001.<ref>(a) {{citation |url=https://www.cup.lmu.de/de/departments/chemie/personen/prof-dr-wolfgang-steglich-em/?lang=default|title=Website Prof. Dr. W. Steglich, LMU Munich, with short CV (English)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912192046/https://www.cup.lmu.de/en/departments/chemistry/people/prof-dr-wolfgang-steglich-em/?lang=default |archive-date=2019-09-12|access-date=2019-09-12|url-status=live}}; (b) {{citation |url=https://www.cup.uni-muenchen.de/oc/steglich/curiculum.php |title=Website Prof. Dr. W. Steglich, LMU Munich, CV (German)|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912192324/https://www.cup.uni-muenchen.de/oc/steglich/curiculum.php |archive-date=2019-09-12 |access-date=2019-09-12 |url-status=live}}.</ref>

==Work==
The use of [[4-dimethylaminopyridine]] for [[esterification]]s with [[anhydride]]s,<ref>{{Cite journal
 | title = 4-Dialkylaminopyridines as Highly Active Acylation Catalysts. &#91;New synthetic method (25)&#93;
 | author = Gerhard Höfle, Wolfgang Steglich, Helmut Vorbrüggen
 | journal=  Angewandte Chemie International Edition in English
 | year = 1978
 | volume = 17
 | pages = 569–583
 | doi = 10.1002/anie.197805691
 | issue = 8}}</ref> which is sometimes called the [[Steglich esterification]], his studies on the metabolism of fungi,
<ref>{{Cite journal
 | title = Pilzfarbstoffe
 | pages = 117–123
 | author = Wolfgang Steglich
 | doi = 10.1002/ciuz.19750090404
 | journal = Chemie in unserer Zeit
 | volume = 9
 | issue = 4
 | year = 1975}}
</ref>
<ref>{{Cite book
 | title = Pigments of Fungi (Macromycetes)
 | pages = 1–317
 | author = Melvyn Gill, Wolfgang Steglich
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-7091-6971-1
 | series = Fortschritte der Chemie organischer Naturstoffe
 | volume = 51
 | year = 1987| isbn = 978-3-7091-7456-2
 }}
{{ISBN|978-3-7091-6971-1}}.
</ref>
and, in collaboration with Timm Anke, the structure elucidation and chemical synthesis of the antifungal [[Strobilurin]]s
<ref>{{Cite journal
 | title = Strobilurins: Evolution of a New Class of Active Substances
 | pages = 1328–1349
 | author = Hubert Sauter, Wolfgang Steglich, Timm Anke
 | journal = Angewandte Chemie International Edition
 | volume = 38
 | year = 1999| issue = 10
 | doi = 10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19990517)38:10<1328::AID-ANIE1328>3.0.CO;2-1
 | pmid = 29711574
 }}
([https://doi.org/10.1002/(SICI)1521-3773(19990517)38:10%3C1328::AID-ANIE1328%3E3.0.CO;2-1 online])
</ref>
that resulted in the industrial development of the novel class of Strobilurin-based crop protection agents
<ref>Peter Jeschke, Matthias Witschel, Wolfgang Krämer, Ulrich Schirmer (eds.), ''Modern Crop Protection Compounds'', 3rd edition, Wiley-VCH, 2019, {{ISBN|978-3-527-34089-7}}.</ref>
are his main contributions in the field of chemistry.
